activity.role: Founding leader and Black Loyalist representative
activity.notes: Thomas Peters was a leading Black Loyalist representative who helped organize the 1792 migration from Nova Scotia to Sierra Leone and was a principal founding figure of Freetown. He did not hold a formal sovereign office over Sierra Leone, so ATLAS records an active_in/general_activity relationship rather than a reign or governorship. 'Sierra Leone Colony' here denotes the Sierra Leone Company-era West African colony centered on the new Freetown settlement, not the later Crown Colony established in 1808.

sources.title: Thomas Peters National Historic Person (c. 1738–1792) — Parks Canada
sources.citation_text: Parks Canada identifies Thomas Peters as a prominent Black Loyalist leader who recruited settlers for Sierra Leone and helped found Freetown in 1792.
